params.place: on the map: the whole Mediterranean, half of it already dry salt flats, a last blue lake shrinking in the middle

moments.what: MEDITERRANEAN SEA writes across the water
the waterline slips back from the coasts
the camera pushes in on the dry floor
salt crystals glitter across the flats

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why would the Mediterranean Sea turn into a desert of salt?

params.place: on the map: the whole sea full again, the camera on its western end

moments.what: the sea floods back to full
a stamp ONCE drops on the sea
the camera slides west
the gap between Europe and Africa glows
GIBRALTAR writes on beside the gap

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It already did, once, and it all hangs on one gap at Gibraltar.

params.place: on the map: the Strait of Gibraltar close, Spain above, Morocco below, a ruler across the gap

moments.what: a ruler swings across the strait
the width tag stamps on the ruler
two door posts stand on either shore
ATLANTIC writes on to the west
waves roll on the ocean side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That gap is just 14.2 kilometres wide, the sea's only door to the open Atlantic Ocean.

params.place: on the map: the sea under a hot sun, rivers flowing in, the Atlantic current pouring through the strait

moments.what: a hot sun rises over the sea
steam curls up off the water
the steam drifts away
the Nile and the Rhone flow in, small
their water trickles into the sea
the camera slides to the strait
arrows of Atlantic water pour through the gap
the gap flashes red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The sun takes more water from this sea than its rivers bring, so the Atlantic keeps pouring in. So what if that door closed?

params.place: on the map: the strait, a dam of land rising across it, a year counter on a rock

moments.what: a stone tablet with the years rises on the shore
the map turns old and sepia
the land on both sides creeps together
the land closes the gap with a thud and dust
the Atlantic arrows stop

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: About 5.96M years ago, that door slammed shut.

params.place: on the map: the whole sea under a blazing sun, the water level dropping

moments.what: a lock stamps on the closed strait
the sun blazes bigger
a gauge on the shore shows the yearly loss
steam pours off the whole sea
the waterline drops a step
the dry riverbeds shrink to trickles
the waterline drops another step

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Cut off, the sun took 3,300 cubic kilometres of water a year, and almost nothing came in to replace it.

params.place: on the map: the coasts of the sea drying one after another, lakes left in the deep basins

moments.what: a year counter flips
it flips again
the Adriatic dries
the Aegean dries
salt crusts spread over the floor
salt crusts thicken along the old coasts
the camera pulls back on a few blue lakes left
SALT LAKES writes on over the deep basins

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Year after year, coast after coast, the water pulled back, leaving only salty lakes in the deepest basins.

params.place: on the map: the Nile's mouth in Egypt, the river cutting a canyon north across the dry floor

moments.what: the Nile glints as it flows north
NILE writes on beside it
the river's end runs north after the waterline
a canyon cuts open along its path
the camera pushes into the canyon walls
the river spills onto the salt floor

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Rivers like the Nile chased the falling water, carving deep canyons down to the new floor.

params.place: on the map: the empty basin, salt flats far below the old shoreline, a cut-away edge showing the depth

moments.what: the last lakes shrink
the volume tank starts draining
the volume tank on the shore empties
the old shoreline glows as a dashed line
salt crystals glitter on the floor
a depth line drops from the shore to the floor
the camera eases back over the basin
a question mark pops over the basin

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Until most of its 3.7M cubic kilometres were gone, leaving a salt desert kilometres deep. So how did the sea ever come back?

params.place: on the map: the land bridge at Gibraltar cracking, the Atlantic spilling over it

moments.what: the stone tablet turns to the new date
the Atlantic rises against the land bridge
the bridge cracks and water bursts through
a waterfall foams down into the basin
the water runs over the rock
the flood starts spreading east

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then, about 5.33M years ago, the Atlantic broke back in at Gibraltar, spilling over the rock.

params.place: on the map: the whole basin, the flood racing east from Gibraltar

moments.what: a flow gauge pops up at the strait
the water front races east
the flow figure lands on the gauge
the gauge needle hits the top
the camera pulls back as the front sweeps across the basin
the water reaches the far coasts
the whole sea is blue again

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By one estimate it roared in at up to 100M cubic metres every second, filling the sea within two years.

params.place: on the map: the whole Mediterranean, full, the gap at Gibraltar closing and the waterline slipping back as the hook opens

moments.what: one half of the sea turns to salt
the other half glows blue
a pointer swings between them
the camera turns to Gibraltar
the land closes the gap
the waterline starts slipping back from the coasts

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Salt desert or blue sea: which would you visit? Because close that one gap again, and the sea starts to drain.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
